questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, make sure that:

options.text: The emergency exits are difficult to open.
The emergency exit warning devices work properly.
The emergency exits are not accessible from inside the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: The emergency exit warning devices work properly.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection, check that emergency exit warning devices work. All emergency exits must open smoothly, be undamaged, and close securely from inside.

questions.question: A properly adjusted flat mirror should let the driver see:

options.text: The rear tires touching the ground.
The front tires touching the ground.
Only the roadway and no parts of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rear tires touching the ground.
questions.explanation: A properly adjusted flat mirror on a school bus lets the driver see 200 feet behind the bus, the base of each rear wheel, and the sides of the bus.

questions.question: Drivers should stop ____ away from students at a bus stop.
questions.explanation: A school bus should stop at least 10 feet away from students being picked up. This makes students walk toward the bus, so the driver can watch their movements and know where they are.

questions.question: If the bus has flashing lights, how far before a bus stop should the lights be turned on?
questions.explanation: If a school bus has alternating flashing amber warning lights, turn them on at least 200 feet before the stop, unless state law requires something different.

questions.question: If equipped, a header board should:

options.text: Be strong enough to hold cargo.
Light up when the engine starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be strong enough to hold cargo.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection, check that the header board is secure, has no damage, and is strong enough to hold cargo.

questions.question: About how many seconds before a bus stop should warning lights be turned on?
questions.explanation: If a school bus has alternating amber warning lights, turn them on at least 200 feet before the stop, which is about five to ten seconds.

questions.question: If a student drops an item while walking to the bus, the student should:

options.text: Stop and pick up the object.
Have another student pick up the object.
Ask the driver to pick up the object.
Just leave the item alone and walk away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask the driver to pick up the object.
questions.explanation: It is dangerous for students to pick up dropped items because the driver might not see them. If an item is dropped, the student should move out of the bus danger zones, get the driver's attention, and ask the driver to get the item.

questions.question: When approaching a bus stop, students on the bus should:

options.text: Stand up and collect their belongings.
Walk to the front of the bus and prepare to exit.

questions.explanation: Students on a school bus should stay seated until told to move. It is unsafe for students to walk around while the bus is moving.

questions.question: Loading passengers onto a school bus:
questions.explanation: More students are killed during loading and unloading than while riding the bus. School bus drivers must follow safety procedures during these times. Proper supervision and care are critical.

questions.question: A school bus must be evacuated if:

options.text: The bus has stalled in winter weather.
The air conditioning system has broken.
There is any immediate danger of collision.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is any immediate danger of collision.
questions.explanation: Usually it is safest for students to stay on the bus during emergencies. Evacuate the bus if it stalls on railroad tracks, if there is fire or threat of fire, if there is a hazardous materials spill, or if there is immediate danger of collision.

questions.question: What is the proper way to use an emergency roof hatch?

options.text: Always lock it down before traveling.
You can leave it partially open while traveling to get fresh air.
Never open it except in an emergency.
Always keep it open while traveling.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can leave it partially open while traveling to get fresh air.
questions.explanation: School bus emergency roof hatches can be locked in a partially open position to allow fresh air inside. Do not make this a regular practice. Remember that an open hatch gives the bus slightly more clearance.

questions.question: Where are the danger zones on a school bus?

options.text: In the front of the bus
To the sides of the bus
To the front, rear, and sides of the bus

questions.correctAnswerText: To the front, rear, and sides of the bus
questions.explanation: Danger zones are areas where children are most likely to be hit by another vehicle or by the bus itself. These areas are in front, on the sides, and behind the bus.

questions.question: When can you proceed across a drawbridge with a traffic signal?

options.text: Only after you stop 50 feet before the bridge.
Only if other vehicles are also going across.
Only after you get out to check the conditions.

questions.explanation: If a drawbridge has a green traffic signal, you can slow down and proceed without stopping.

questions.question: When should you remind passengers to take their carry-on bags when leaving the bus?
questions.explanation: Tell passengers to take their carry-on bags before you bring the bus to a complete stop at the destination.

questions.question: During exercises other than straight line backing, how many times can you exit your vehicle to check its position?
questions.explanation: You can exit your vehicle to check its position during a basic control skills test. This is called a "look." For straight line backing, you may look only once. For any other exercise, you may look no more than twice.

questions.question: What tool should you use to check if tires have the right amount of air?
questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge during the vehicle inspection test to check tire air pressure. Simply kicking the tires will not pass the test.

questions.question: What should you be able to see when convex mirrors are properly adjusted?

options.text: Where the front of each rear tire touches the ground.
Where the front of each front tire touches the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where the front of each rear tire touches the ground.
questions.explanation: Properly adjusted convex mirrors on a school bus should show at least one traffic lane on each side, the entire side of the bus, and where the front of each rear tire touches the ground.

questions.question: How far behind the bus should properly adjusted mirrors allow you to see?
questions.explanation: Proper mirror adjustment is important for safe bus operation. The bus's flat mirrors should be adjusted so you can see 200 feet (about four bus lengths) behind the bus.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, which of the following will you NOT have to do?

options.text: Point to or touch each item.
Explain what you are checking and why.

questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must walk around the vehicle, point to or touch each item, and explain what you are checking and why. You do not need to crawl under the hood or under the vehicle.

questions.question: If you must stop before making a turn during the skills test, what should you do?

options.text: Stop after the stop line to see better.
Keep the front wheels aimed straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the front wheels aimed straight ahead.
questions.explanation: Make a smooth stop behind any stop line, crosswalk, or stop sign. Keep your front wheels straight and do not let your vehicle roll. If stopping behind another vehicle, stop where you can still see its rear tires.
